title: Volodymyr Zelensky, the great escape artist
gist: Andrew Adonis argues Zelensky is surviving a Trump-Putin diesel deal and Trump's calls for a new Ukrainian president thanks to European backing and drones hitting Russian refineries. He expects a ceasefire roughly on current lines.

insights.claim: Trump announced a diesel deal with Putin that dismantles US trade sanctions on Russia and finances Russia's war machine, reversing the policy of strangling the Russian economy.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Sanctions relief on Russian diesel would be a major shift for energy and sanctions positioning.
insights.locator: When Trump’s diesel deal with Putin

insights.claim: The proposed Russian diesel sales cover only a tiny fraction of US requirements to bring down pump prices amid the Iran war, and experts consider them probably unattainable given Russian needs and Ukrainian refinery strikes.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Limits the real supply impact on fuel prices, so diesel-price relief via Russia is unlikely.

insights.claim: Trump said 'it's time for Ukraine to get a new president' and told Zelensky to stop bombing Russian oil refineries.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Heightens the risk of US policy swinging against Kyiv.
insights.quote: I think it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president

insights.claim: Ukraine's new drones are systematically disabling Russian oil refineries hundreds of miles away, and Putin has made no notable advance since the February Oval Office clash.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Refinery strikes cut Russian product exports and tighten diesel markets.

insights.claim: Zelensky's drone production does not depend on US permissions, so an 'energy ceasefire' Putin has not agreed to will not be observed by Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure will likely continue.
insights.locator: whose drone production doesn’t depend on US permissions

insights.claim: Europe's leaders have substituted for American financial aid, and changes of European leadership have either not affected or helped Ukraine support, as with Orban's defeat and Meloni's strengthening.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: European fiscal support for Ukraine appears durable.

insights.claim: Adonis doubts a Le Pen/Bardella government after France's May presidential election would break European support for Ukraine, noting they denounced Russian 'hostile acts'.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Lowers the risk that French politics undermines European unity on Ukraine.

insights.claim: Adonis considers the most likely end to the war a ceasefire along roughly present occupation lines, which he calls a triumph preserving four-fifths of Ukraine as an independent European state.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Frozen-front ceasefire is the base case for reconstruction and sanctions planning.
insights.locator: The most likely end to the war

insights.claim: US mid-term elections within 60 days will very likely weaken Trump, giving Zelensky another break.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Midterm results are a catalyst for US Ukraine policy.
